item.title: Re: SCP Idea - seeking greenlight
item.content:encoded:
Hey there Snow Lily, I'll be critting your idea today!
Note that I am not an official reviewer (though I am a flight officer), so take everything I say with a grain of salt. With that being said, let's begin the (brief) crit!

+ Open Section-by-Section +
- Close Section-by-Section -

Elevator Pitch

Immediately, I'm seeing a big problem here: your concept's anomalous property is both 1)extremely overpowered and 2)contrived to be a pain for the Foundation (oddly specific). Firstly, while being OP isn't necessarily a bad thing, it requires excellent execution. Otherwise, the article starts seeming less like a scientific document and more like a detailed description of a comic book superhero/supervillain, breaking the reader's suspension of disbelief and causing the anomaly to seem slightly ridiculous. Secondly, the ability of controlling other SCPs specifically seems contrived and convenient. Why is it only able to control SCPs? And while we're on that topic, how does it know about the Foundation? And to restate Kingyo's question, why did it try to release the SCPs?

Central Narrative

Nothing I'm seeing in this section impresses me. Basically, the anomaly tries and fails to break all the SCPs out of containment, and proceeds to clam up when asked why. The end. It just restates the anomaly's abilities and we proceed to learn absolutely nothing new. No backstory, no interesting application of the ability, no twist, subversion, or reveal. Narratives should make the reader feel something, and this makes me feel nothing (except boredom).

Hook/Attention Grabber

This is a mystery which you hang in front of us with no way whatsoever of getting closer to solving it. It is technically a mystery, but quite poorly designed, as there is neither lead-up, emotional attachment to this anomaly or story, or way to solve it.

+ Open General Thoughts +
I'm quite doubtful about this, I'm afraid

This anomaly suffers from something I'm going to call 'Blank God Complex', wherein the anomaly is quite powerful (or in this case, OP) but lacks a proper narrative. This is quite a bad thing to have, as narrative is one of the most important parts of the newer Series VI, to the point where a narrative is not only simply expected to exist, but expected to be high-quality (which I'm all for). One more thing to consider: this is a humanoid anomaly, one of the most difficult types of anomaly to write by a significant margin.
Anyway, I'd recommend four things:
1. Reworking your anomaly's ability slightly, as it seems manufactured to be a problem for the Foundation (as a bonus drawback, this contrived nature gives me self-insert vibes, which isn't good)
2. Overhauling your story. Find an emotion you want us readers to feel, and then create a story around that.
3. Check out the Guide Hub for some great articles and essays to help with ideation and story-ing!
4. Contact someone from the Butterfly Squad. They've got tons of experience and are really helpful!

And finally, to sum up your idea in one sentence1:
A humanoid that is able to control all other SCPs around it, simply by saying 'control'.

Anyway, that's it for my crit. Thanks for reading, and I hope this helps!
P.S Don't hesitate to PM me if you change your anomaly. I might be a couple of days, but I'll try my best for a recrit! Just make sure to link this thread so that I don't have to hunt for it in the forums.

Footnotes
1. This is to help you get a more objective look at your concept from the point of view of a critter. You may find something you don't like here, or that we're getting the wrong impression.

item.title: Re: DECEMBER 2020 INTROS - Explorers
item.content:encoded:
Hello everyone! I'm Ross - although you can call me Mira too, if you'd like!

I'm 20 years old, and I've been been a casual reader of SCP articles for what must be almost five or six years now. Recently, though, I've delved far deeper into the assorted canons and some of the less "popular" articles, and I'm amazed by just how much the site really has to offer.

I enjoy the tone of the SCP Wiki on the whole - the general style is one that I am not particularly good at writing, but enjoy reading to a great extent. The creativity on display in exploring concepts from the harmlessly light-hearted to the ones so horrifying that they have stuck with me for years is nothing short of admirable. (Perhaps one day, I'll workshop an idea of my own, but that isn't likely to happen for a very long time.)

As far as hobbies go, I enjoy character design and writing, and as some have likely deduced from my username, I'm a huge fan of visual novels as well. I also like baking, although most baked goods tend to be a little too sweet for my personal tastes.

With regards to what kind of random thoughts keep me up at night, they tend to range from something as mundane as having a song stuck in my head to whatever catastrophic situations my tired, anxious mind is able to come up with. Typically, though, they'll just jump from one topic of interest to another - usually if I've read something I really enjoyed, I won't be able to stop thinking about it.

item.title: Re: Psychological Theories in 1800s
item.content:encoded:
So uh… This may or may not be useful, but as I'm sure you know, in the nineteenth century there were all kinds of crazy "cures" for mental illness. One that really stands out as particularly crazy was called the Cox's Chair. It was basically a chair you would strap someone in, then spin the chair around really, really fast. (Like spinning in an office chair, except more intense.) You would then stop the chair suddenly, in the hope that the illness would be forcefully jerked out of the patient. (It didn't work) So if what you were looking for was an entity that tries to help people, but sort of… screws up, Cox's Chair could be an interesting edition. I hope you find what you're looking for, and good luck on your scip!

item.title: Re: Looking for Greenlights | The Stardust Solution
item.content:encoded:
1) A minor problem is that this makes another reset option and that it has been used twice before. If it hadn't been tied in to "narrative", it wouldn't have been noticed.

2) As a science geek, there's my usual issue involving singularities: Their very presence planetside should be causing a lot of problems, especially one that's going to go Big Bang. If it's just going to increase its density, then that means that it's going to be a problem well before it explodes. That is was found with just a stone tablet just makes it even sillier (if it sucks in nearby matter/energy at a subatomic level, why would the stone tablet last that long?).

3) Given the sheer number of alien races and dimensional links that the SCP deals with, this is not as big a problem as it may seem: Just have an alien race looking for a power source pick it up or dimensionally displace it to a dead universe. If the alien that put it down comes around looking for it, just give him the coordinates.

It's a neat idea, but it's going to be neutralized quickly. It has to be.

item.title: Re: Thaumiel Factory Failure (seeking greenlight)
item.content:encoded:
Responded:

+ show block
– hide block

They don't. They simply try to manufacture Objects that could aid the foundation, who would then in turn be classified as Thaumiel.

Not all objects that could be helpful are given the Thaumiel class. If this person is only churning out items that would be considered Thaumiel, that's a difficult to believe level of specificity and ability.

This is the reason this individual does not speak to the foundation at all while building the factory. They want the products to speak for themselves.

Again, why would they assume the Foundation would use the products to begin with, especially if they don't have any insight into the production and motive behind the items?

he thinks that the foundation in its entirety is completely good and would never do anything evil.

Given that the Foundation would have had to be ridiculously sloppy in order for the person to witness a single event that makes them understand that there's a whole shadow organization that is intent on containing the anomalous, this is difficult to believe. You as the author inherently know everything ahead of time, but your character needs to learn in a believable manner if you want the audience to take the story seriously.

This Person does not happen to have it. He builds it himself. How he does that is something I am still working on. Plan is currently that he uses his money to hire people that know a thing or two and compiles their knowledge.

The issue with this is that it's overpowered and contrived. You have so many unlikely elements already, the fact that the guy inherits money, the fact that he wasn't noticed by the Foundation during a containment event, the fact that he hires people to make anomalies somehow, and so on. Each of these traits separately is already potentially skepticism-raising; combining so many of these coincidences just makes for a story that feels sloppily made up and fake.

things he thinks are useful like gloves that make your hands indestructable, boxes that lock things inside with no way of opening them from the inside, glasses that protect your mind from seeing things and hazmat suits to keep nasty stuff away.

Since none of these things can be reliably used to observably contain anomalies, they wouldn't be classified as Thaumiel.

I want the factory to have 1 important person in charge, who hired other people to help him build it, yet him pulling all the strings.

This doesn't answer my question of why you want only one person.

I am open to any changes that make the story better/clearer without completely changing its direction.

I feel like for this to stand more of a chance with the audience, you need to change the following:

  • don't have just one person in charge. Have at least two or three friends/family members. If you just have one person, they'll seem like a too-important overpowered Mary Sue character.
  • don't have them witness a Foundation containment and somehow go unnoticed. Have someone they are close to be involved in an incident, and maybe taken into Foundation custody. When the person goes looking, they find a Foundation agent checking up on the amnesticized someone and the agent gives some very brief information about being with an organization that "helps after disasters" or something. Your character talks to their friend/whoever who was in the incident, and wants to start helping the people who saved their friend/whoever. This will make more sense than your current setup.
  • don't have the setup be for a factory, which implies mass production and cut corners for many exact copies of the same product. Use "workshop" or the like. This will make the Foundation more interested in testing the items as individual anomalies rather than just locking all of the stuff up as repeat junk.

There will definitely be more changes needed after these, but that's what I would start with.

item.title: Re: A draft featuring the Village People, Shrunken Heads, Neurotoxins and Clickbait
item.content:encoded:
I'm speechless. This draft is utterly ridiculous, not-at-all serious, and a complete joke. And the best comedic scip I've read yet. Seriously, how has no one commented on this? The final log is one of the best things about it. You set up a (semi)realistic scenario with the cops, and then turn everything on its head with a cosmic entity. I only have one real question. Why has the Foundation not attempted to use this to help contain/slow down dangerous scips? Although you definitely have enough material, a short addenda talking about perhaps the results of some tests on other scips could provide a comedic sharp contrast between the incident report and a bit of dry, humorless test results. But yes, I certainly found it lovely to read, and you kept me chuckleing the entire time.

item.title: Re: Blood Storm
item.content:encoded:
1) You have something that covers roughly 270,000 square miles and you think that The Foundation has enough amnestics to deal with the situation? And that ANYONE can keep THAT a secret? Yeah, it ain't happening. You need to shrink this by a lot.

2) No conversion back is possible? Again, if you're trying to keep this a secret, this ain't working. Even if you shrink the size of this down to a city, that's still a lot of transformed individuals that the MTFs aren't getting to and will be around well after the fact. You're going to have a couple of organizations looking to snag a couple of the individuals as weapons for later.

The quicky solution is that the transformation only lasts a few hours after the rain, possibly with individuals that have been in the rain lasting a little longer. Otherwise, you're going to have a lot aggressive individuals to account for.

3) With this much chaos, there has to be a way to predict where it's going to be or it's going to be causing a lot of problems, even if it's only every four years.

item.title: Re: "The Man of Nobody"
item.content:encoded:
Hello caspian2, thank you for responding! I appreciate the interest in the concept. After speaking in the IRC chat I discussed and most people said that due to the nature of this anomaly it would make sense if he developed it around 13~ when he went through his first breakup, however that wouldn't explain why the anomaly itself occured. I foolishly didn't preemptively think of how that'd be. I'll begin to brainstorm how to improve on the concept of how the anomaly was gained. I made a specific vow to not crosslink SCPs so I can't use another person's SCP, as I don't want to seem as if I'm riding off of their success - especially since this is my first SCP.

The reason they'd die the painful deaths is due to the curse/anomaly affected SCP-XXXX, which I still need to decide the cause of. I should be more specific and say that it's an extremely painful death - the pain dependent on how strong the mentioned relationship. Yes, acquaintance counts as a relationship. However it's only under verbal or written recognition where the effect appears. So if it simply isn't mentioned then it'll be fine.

With suicide patients, usually they can be sent to mental wards or the like to receive therapy. Inside of this therapy, usually catered towards people with extreme mental disorders, the main way which they're assisted by psychologists is via forming a strong, trusting relationship with them. However, he quite obviously can't do that.

I also decided during the time of discussion in the IRC chat that they actually turned themselves into the SCP foundation. I'd need to choose how they discovered the SCP Foundation, but that's the angle I want. They feel bad for wanting the attention so they try to trap themselves, but still get desperate and try to escape.

Due to Leveritas' advice, I've also decided to make a non-humanoid SCP first as that'd probably be a better way to start myself off. Thank you for the advice - I'll remember it for when I return to the concept later on in time.

item.title: [Seeking Greenlights] What Follows
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch:
"What Follows" is, to put it in the most basic terms possible, what makes you need to run up the stairs whenever it is dark. The SCP itself is theorized to reside in the human psychospace, which is why it is such a widespread phenomenon among humans. While the SCP itself is the feeling of fear when walking up a dark staircase, the actual danger of it comes from it's secondary instance, which attacks whichever unfortunate person has chosen to not run up the stairs in time (Not always resulting in death).

Central Narrative:
Containment procedures begin the article with the possibility of the SCP residing in the human psychospace, as well as the fact that the primary instance of the SCP cannot be contained, with the Foundation's main way of containment being a public misinformation campaign. Throughout the article, it is increasingly alluded to that the SCP is more than a simple fight-or-flight response to a monster under the stairs, but could be a breakthrough in unlocking greater human potential, ad even the ability to see into the near future.

Collaps'd (More below)
Uncollaps'd

Most of the following would be shown through addendums and interview logs:
With the possibility of such important breakthroughs, upper foundation staff decide to begin a special research project on the matter. The actual project name is redacted, giving the reader the possibility that it may actually be project PNEUMA (and therefor might lead to the O-5's decision to terminate humanity). The actual end result of the project isn't revealed, with it only being alluded to that it didn't go well, so that the reader is left with a sense of mystery as to exactly what the foundation learned.

Hook/Attention-Grabber:
Just to start off, the article opens with a note from the Containment Committee on reallocating more staff towards the research of this entity, as well as the Containment Procedure itself stating that the primary instance of the SCP cannot be contained.

Additional Notes:
I've never been good at voicing my thoughts, so just to make it clear: The SCP is the feeling of fear itself when walking up a dark staircase, with it's secondary instance being the actual attack from behind.

FredEx, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

Also, if your brother is co-authoring your piece, please provide his username so you can credit him for his contributions properly. Furthermore, please note that the SCP wiki does not allow accounts to be shared.

item.title: Re: Good intentions
item.content:encoded:
Please note that I am not the most experienced user. Please reach out to veterans for some more-informed crit.

On the whole, I'm not convinced that this is ready for the drafting process. You've clearly thought out some of the themes and ideas that you want to express with the SCP, but you don't do anything particularly interesting with them. The long bit that you've put in the "Narrative" section isn't a narrative at all, it's just a lot of detail about how the thing works, which at this stage is pretty unnecessary. Name dropping the Broken God tells me that either A: this DOES have a narrative and you're not elaborating on it (in which case do that), or B: you're trying to make it more interesting purely by tying in an existing entity, which will never get you far unless your piece was thought out beforehand as a meaningful addition to that body of work.

I would recommend mulling this over a bit more to see if there's really a story here that you want to tell. If not, then it would probably be easier to start from scratch, building the anomaly around the narrative rather than vice versa.

have a good day!

item.title: Re: The Boy Who Can Do Anything (Looking For Green Lights)
item.content:encoded:
You typed that the dog was there to apparently defuse the kid; how does he do that?

The problem is simply that the kid feels more like a MacGuffin than an actual character: There's a problem, the kid shows up, problem solved, if he gets out of hand a dog shows up to slow him down.

We already have that in SCP-343 (assuming He's who He says he is); but that character is still a character. We need some way of differentiating this guy from any other MacGuffin and that's usually through its personality.

This guy needs a lot of work, but if you can start with the personality and go from there it should be a lot easier for you.

item.title: Re: The Silver Sludge
item.content:encoded:
This is more of a combination of different ideas, but from a technological side. The problem here is that while you created an interesting monster, its personality needs to be straightened out: Is it terrified of people, is it trying to purify the world, is it purifying because it's terrified? Pick a personality and go for it.

You also need to give some backstory: What created this thing? Where did it come from? Why does it want to purify the world? What does it have against free will? What will it replace that with? Basically, we know what it does; we need to why it does what it does. Even if it's just a lab experiment gone really, really wrong that wants to prevent other such beings from being created, that's still an origin.

Lastly, we need to have a reason to care about it. How does it fit in with the greater SCP-U? Does it make a particular point or is just there? We need to have a reason to care about the critter.

Good luck!

item.title: House of Memories
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Page Layout: Just your typical SCP article layout. Some interviews, some exploration logs, maybe a few notes, I dunno. That's something for me to handle during the drafting phase.

As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices...
...please collapse long posts.

Elevator Pitch: A house that causes you to experience past memories (or just past experiences in your life, doesn't really matter if you remember it). It'll normally attempt to lure you in by using creatures that trick you into believing that people you trust are asking you to go inside, primarily by shapeshifting. The main creature1 luring you in is trapped inside the house and can create other creatures2 to go outside and lure you in for it if necessary. It will keep trying until it gets tired or finds more suitable prey. Once you're in, you become one of the minions of the main creature inhabiting the house.

Central Narrative: So… some kids messed up. Basically, a kid's grandmother told him about a spell that could curse households. Reason? Not important. What's important is that you can't trust kids with magic. That kid went and told all his friends about it, and they thought it would be funny if they cursed this one house on a mountain.

Oh yeah, did I mention kids are really bad at using magic? In fact, they're so bad that one of the kids in the friend group got cursed along with the house and was forced to inhabit it forever3. After the spell was cast, the Foundation detected anomalous activity on a mountain… somewhere. Haven't decided yet. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Anyway, the Foundation took the kids in and gave them amnestics, but… it didn't work. Because of how the curse functions, it wouldn't allow them to forget about it. The Foundation had no choice but to take care of them until they were old enough to become Class-D Personnel.

All of those events set up the Foundation's investigations on why the house was what it was. The Class-D were used for explorations and it revealed more about the grandmother (yeah, remember her?) and her relations to their family's history with magic and anomalies.

Hook/Attention Grabber: I guess it could be the small mistake of some negligent kids unraveling a family's anomalous secrets. The chain reaction could be somewhat interesting.

Additional Notes: While ambitious for a first-time SCP writer, the magical history of the family could be a nice setup for a GoI. I wouldn't get too excited about that yet though. :)

Also, I would like some attention on my hook, as I'm kind of struggling with it.

Footnotes
1. SCP-XXXX-1
2. SCP-XXXX-2 instances
3. This is SCP-XXXX-1

item.title: SCP-The Mimic
item.content:encoded:
Seeking Greenlights: Yes

Page Type: SCP Article

Elevator Pitch: The SCP is a humanoid entity similar to SCP-096, being tall, disproportionate, and skinny. The SCP can produce any sound at any volume at any location, as long as it's heard it before. There are also two other parts of the SCP. The village it came from is the first, it's an endless maze of houses and shops, some buildings being made of obscure materials, including glass, wires, and human components. The other part of the SCP are people who have seen the entity through photography or video. The go crazy a few hours after seeing the image or video, and kill any living thing they see, but can't die themselves.

Central Narrative: After reports came that an entire village had been wiped out, the foundation investigated, and found the entity in the forest near by, and brought it into containment. They also discovered the anomalous effects of the village. Then, after taking pictures of the SCP, and showing them to a few people, those people went crazy, and those anomalous effects were discovered.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: The physical description, and the ability of the entity grabs attention, as it's very obscure and slightly scary. The description and ability of the village and the crazy people also add to it, as they are also pretty freaky, and generally disturbing. It may not be extremely significant, but it adds as a whole to the scp world.

item.title: Re: (Looking for greenlight) Ancient elevators
item.content:encoded:
+ Open for critique
- Behold!

I absolutely love this. As I was reading I was concerned that this lacked a punchline, but you cleared that quickly.

A few points of advice.
Make sure that list of elevators does not drag and has a rise in bizarreness. You shouldn't start with the pyramids or a recognizable location. You should also expound upon how these machines work, mainly for world building and such. There's some cool imagery here that could be fun reading.

I'm not sure an MTF log is exactly needed. That could be taking up unnecessary space to establish team members, what they're doing, and so on before all the action. Keep the whole satellite detection point, but just have a Foundation doctor communicate over a transmission system of some sort. You should be going for the energy of SCP-3197.

I do feel like the aliens landing on Earth is unneeded. If their whole MO was to "uplift" the human species, them coming back every, say, 1000 years to monitor the Earth would make a bit more sense and also explain why the Foundation has never interacted with them before.

Definite greenlight from me. Good luck and be sure to reach out to other reviewers!

item.title: Re: SCP Greenlight Idea
item.content:encoded:
This has some similarities to SCP-2128, with that being a bit more interesting due to the historical aspect and the present anomalous properties.

As for you're, I really don't find this interesting. Everything past the cage-like appearance seems cliche: two states, torture, murder, and only moving when not seen. This needs to be developed, mainly to answer the question why? Why does this thing do what it does? This doesn't have to be a full origin story, more along the lines of something to contextualize the anomaly in a way that will either induce more horror or allow the reader to understand something further.

While I find the feeding off of pain aspect somewhat interesting, if this is a predator that eats its prey, why does it go through the trouble of touting the prey, releasing it, then eating it? It feels too convoluted to where I'm now thinking that the other bear form should be cut entirely. Have the crate be the entire anomaly, it draws in prey, tortures them, and eats them. The torturing part does feel slightly overboard, but perhaps that's just me.

As of right now, this will not get a greenlight from me.

item.content:encoded:
I will revise this article a bit, thank you for the advice. I could've been a bit more clear at different points and I will attempt to clarify a bit in this here as well:
-It is a "sound" that has a roughly 2 km radius, emanating at about 432.7 Hz.
-Said sound cannot be picked up by any equipment, only by human ears (including the deaf) and cannot be impeded by any earmuffs either.
-The "sound" is mobile, so effects of long term exposure are relatively unknown (also making it hard to contain as it moves in random directions at about a 3km/hr pace)
-I think the narrative arc I was looking for was sort of the conflict of the foundation trying to contain said anomaly by burying it while (and I suppose it doesn't have to be AWCY it can just be assorted musicians I just thought it may fit their whole vibe) others attempt to create some sort of art with it, playing music that harmonizes with the frequency.

I will admit this isn't my strongest concept, it needs some revision and I'm still not 100% sure what the core narrative is, however the central premise I'm trying to go off of is the idea that the foundation invests a large amount of resources into containing this relatively benign anomaly, while other people/groups are able to use it in a way that is more for entertainment or art. If that's a weak premise I'll drop the idea and move on to something else though

item.title: SCP-XXXX Where the Heart is
item.content:encoded:
Shared pain and experiences can bring people closer together, who doesn't want that!? Something else wants to attain its former glory - there seem to be some "win-win" situations here.

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlights: Yes
Page Type: SCP Article
Genre: Horror?

Elevator Pitch:

  • A creature that haunts Christmas as well as Halloween
  • Object Class: Keter For its innumerable ways of evading capture, enclosures, and personnel
  • There are three types of encounters (with the main entity specifically), they are:
    • Black Events: Where the ritualistic consumption of a child is done by the child's family, along with the entity during Halloween
    • White Events: Causes a family to become closer to each other as serial murders after SCP-XXXX is taken in (while posing as a homeless person)
    • Red Events: Are when it's outside of a Black or White Event and gouges out the heart of a person(s)
+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative: The creature was once one of the "Faces of the Holidays", namely Halloween. With a competitive and impulsive nature, it ate the heart of "Christmas" - becoming a being that encompasses both holidays. Though this caused it to become even more unstable, now consuming the hearts of 'innocents' to regain its purity in its madness.

Hook/Attention-Grabber: While the creature seems very violent, it sometimes leaves people better than before: having a better outlook on life and being an overall better person.

Don't let that small chance of salvation fool you though - while its intentions may not be evil, what it does is extremely traumatizing.

Additional Notes: I did NOT include all of the context/info with these events and capabilities to make it easily digestible in this format.

This is my first time making one of these… so yeah, thanks for reading and tell me if there's anything I did wrong here; or if there are any questions :)


As a courtesy to our readers on mobile devices, please collapse long posts and properly space your paragraphs. ~Zyn
